mainEntity.name: Can dental implants be placed if I have gum disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active gum disease typically needs treatment before implant placement to ensure optimal healing and long-term success. Professional assessment can determine the appropriate treatment sequence, which may include periodontal therapy followed by tissue healing before implant surgery. Controlled gum disease doesn't necessarily prevent implant treatment, but addressing inflammation first improves predictability and outcomes.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for gums to heal and shape around implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Initial gum healing around implants typically occurs within the first few weeks, but complete tissue maturation and final contour development can take several months. During this period, the gums gradually adapt to the implant and develop stable, healthy contours. Some minor changes in gum shape may continue for up to a year as the tissues fully integrate with the implant restoration.

mainEntity.name: Will my gums look natural around a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern implant techniques and careful attention to gum architecture typically achieve very natural-looking results. The final appearance depends on factors including initial tissue quality, proper implant positioning, and adequate healing time. When necessary, tissue enhancement procedures can be used to optimise gum contours and create more natural-looking results that blend seamlessly with surrounding teeth.

mainEntity.name: Can gums recede around dental implants like natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: While gums can experience some recession around implants, healthy tissue maintained through good oral hygiene typically remains stable long-term. Unlike natural teeth, implants don't have the same biological attachment to gums, making proper tissue health particularly important. Regular professional monitoring and excellent home care help prevent complications that might lead to tissue recession.

mainEntity.name: Do I need special care for my gums after getting implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gum care around implants requires similar attention to natural teeth but may benefit from specific techniques. Daily cleaning around the implant site, regular professional monitoring, and prompt attention to any inflammation help maintain healthy tissue. Your dental team will provide specific guidance on cleaning techniques and tools that work best for your implant restoration and gum health.

mainEntity.name: Can uneven gums be corrected during implant treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gum contouring and other cosmetic procedures can often be performed in conjunction with implant treatment to improve tissue symmetry and appearance. These procedures help create more even gum lines and better overall aesthetic harmony. The timing and specific techniques depend on individual assessment and treatment planning, with some corrections possible during implant placement and others requiring separate procedures.
